title: Marriage and Divorce: What God Wants and the Hope He Gives
speaker: Aaron Brockett
goal: Facilitate honest conversations about how God redeems broken relationships, including marriage.
scripture_instructions: Have one person read Mark 10:1-12 aloud, then pause for quiet reflection before discussion starts.

icebreakers.label: A
icebreakers.question: What did you want to be when you grew up?
icebreakers.note: Use this to break the ice and build rapport.

icebreakers.label: B
icebreakers.question: Describe a memorable wedding you've attended.
icebreakers.note: This connects personal experiences with the topic.

icebreakers.label: C
icebreakers.question: Share a challenging relationship moment and what it taught you.
icebreakers.note: Encourages vulnerability and sets the tone for deeper discussion.

sections.title: Beginning with Brokenness
sections.setup: The story of Harry and Nellie illustrates how God can bring beauty from the ashes of past mistakes. This sets the stage for understanding the redemptive power of God in our relationships.
sections.say: Let’s start by acknowledging that marriage can be messy and redemption stories remind us that God works in brokenness.

questions.ask: Where have you seen God redeem a situation that seemed hopeless?
questions.lead: Harry's story shows redemption happens beyond initial failures.
questions.probe: What specific action can you take to invite God into your broken places?

questions.ask: How have your family relationships shaped your views on marriage?
questions.lead: Aaron shared his own family history marked by broken marriages.
questions.probe: What beliefs from your upbringing still influence you today?

questions.ask: How do you handle lingering guilt from past relationship failures?
questions.lead: Divorce often leaves scars, but is not the unforgivable sin, according to Aaron.
questions.probe: What steps can you take this week toward accepting grace in those areas?

questions.ask: How has the pain of a past divorce or separation affected you personally?
questions.lead: The sermon illustrated that God hates divorce but loves the people involved.
questions.probe: What forgiveness have you sought or should you offer?

reflection_questions: Where have I seen God redeem a situation that seemed hopeless?
How have my family relationships shaped my views on marriage?
How do I handle lingering guilt from past relationships?
How has the pain of a past divorce affected me personally?

sections.title: Understanding God's Design
sections.setup: In discussing marriage, Jesus emphasized unity and covenant, not just the legality of divorce. God’s design is about lifelong commitment and reflection of His love.
sections.say: Jesus pointed to God's original intent for marriage, unity and covenant.

questions.ask: How do you view marriage differently when you consider it a covenant, not a contract?
questions.lead: Jesus elevated the conversation to God's original intent for marriage.
questions.probe: What's one change you need to make to reflect this view in your own relationship?

questions.ask: When did you have to choose commitment over convenience in a relationship?
questions.lead: Covenant relationships involve deeper commitment and sacrifice than contracts.
questions.probe: How does that choice impact your relationship with God or others today?

questions.ask: Where have you felt cultural pressures against God's design for marriage?
questions.lead: The true purpose of marriage is often challenged in today's culture.
questions.probe: How can you guard your relationship against these influences?

questions.ask: How does understanding marriage in this way affect your current or future relationships?
questions.lead: Marriage was described as a reflection of Jesus' relationship with the church.
questions.probe: In what situation can you better model this relationship?

reflection_questions: How do I view marriage differently when considering it a covenant?
When have I chosen commitment over convenience in a relationship?
Where have I felt cultural pressures against God's design for marriage?
How does understanding marriage as Jesus' reflection affect my relationships?

sections.title: Grace and Redemption
sections.setup: Aaron reminded us that God's grace is abundant, even after relationship failures, and He offers redemption and hope for everyone.
sections.say: Grace allows for second chances. Jesus' interaction with the woman at the well illustrates this redemption.

questions.ask: What steps have you taken to embrace grace in your own life?
questions.lead: God offers grace and redemption no matter the past.
questions.probe: What's the next step you need to take in accepting grace?

questions.ask: Where are you most in need of Jesus' redeeming grace right now?
questions.lead: The woman at the well encountered grace despite her marital history.
questions.probe: How can you actively seek that grace this week?

questions.ask: Where might you be resisting aligning your life with God's design for relationships?
questions.lead: Jesus calls us to respond to His grace by aligning our lives with God's Word.
questions.probe: What's one specific change you can commit to making?

questions.ask: How do you extend grace and forgiveness to yourself and others regularly?
questions.lead: Living in God's grace means embodying forgiveness and surrender.
questions.probe: Who in your life needs more grace from you?

questions.ask: When have you experienced the need to turn from a past mistake and make amends?
questions.lead: Recognition of past mistakes calls for a response of repentance and action.
questions.probe: What immediate steps can you take to address any unresolved issues?

reflection_questions: What steps have I taken to embrace grace in my life?
Where am I most in need of Jesus' grace right now?
Where might I be resisting alignment with God's design?
How do I extend grace to myself and others regularly?
When have I needed to turn from a past mistake and make amends?

closing_go_around: Share one way you're inviting God to work in your relationships this week.
prayer: Pray for strength to approach relationships with grace and for God to redeem the areas that need healing.

cheat_sheet.response: Affirm their vulnerability and discuss how God's grace operates in our brokenness.
Facilitate a discussion about strategies to guard against negative influences.
Redistribute the focus to Jesus' offer of grace and forgiveness.

cheat_sheet.dynamic: Talk turns to doctrine over personal stories.
cheat_sheet.response: Redirect to personal application and lived experiences.
Steer back to the broader theme of grace and redemption.

key_themes: Marriage as a covenant, not a contract.
Overcoming religious contracts with covenant faith.
commitment_prompt: Invite one friend to ask you next week about how you applied today’s discussions in your relationships.
thesis: Marriage is God's covenant, not a contract, and He provides hope and redemption in our brokenness.
sensitivities: Divorce can be a painful subject; approach with empathy.
Some may feel guilt or shame about past relationships.
Not all may agree on biblical grounds for divorce.
obstacle: What usually keeps you from acting in grace and humility towards others?
carry: Ask each other about one specific step you took to align with God's design for relationships.
